a: We introduce the RefNLI benchmark, a dataset featuring 1,143 examples for studying the the effect of reference determinacy in NLI, a common assumption in the creation processes of NLI datasets.
b: The RefNLI benchmark consists of 486 claim-evidence pairs annotated for reference determinacy.
label: contradiction
rationale: Same benchmark, two different sizes (1,143 vs 486).

a: We generally observe that models exhibit low precision and high recall on both contradiction and entailment predictions, suggesting the presence of many false positive predictions made on the two labels.
b: Our finetuned models rarely produce false positive contradiction predictions, achieving high precision on that label.
label: contradiction
rationale: Low precision / many false positives vs high precision / rare false positives, for the same models and label.

a: We observe that apart from the case where true claims are verified against sentences from the correct Wikipedia page, NLI models make contradiction predictions much more frequently than entailments in all the other three cases.
b: In every retrieval setting we examined, entailment was the models' most frequent non-neutral prediction.
label: contradiction
rationale: Contradiction outnumbers entailment in three of four settings, so entailment cannot be the most frequent non-neutral prediction in every setting. Requires mapping 'most frequent non-neutral' onto the contradiction/entailment comparison.

a: On a sub-sample of 102 claims, we ask three authors to produce the label individually and we observe 0.83 Fleiss’ under 4-way classification, suggesting a good inter-rater agreement under the setting.
b: Each of the three authors labelled a separate third of the 102-claim sub-sample, so no claim was labelled more than once.
label: contradiction
rationale: Inter-rater agreement (Fleiss' kappa) requires each claim to be labelled by several raters; disjoint thirds make that impossible. Requires knowing what an agreement statistic needs.

a: To further validate that the reference determinacy assumption in the training data has an impact on downstream performance, we demonstrate that filtering out examples where reference determinacy cannot be easily determined improves the resulting model’s performance on RefNLI .
b: Filtering out training examples whose reference determinacy cannot be easily determined had no effect on the resulting model's performance on RefNLI.
label: contradiction
rationale: The same filtering intervention 'improves' vs 'had no effect on' performance on RefNLI.

a: On five popular NLI datasets ( section 4 ), we demonstrate that different combinations of training datasets result in similar type of reference (in-)determinacy problem in the finetuned model.
b: Our experiments draw on four NLI datasets, which we combine into every possible training mixture.
label: contradiction
rationale: Five datasets vs four datasets for the same experiments.

a: In terms of AUROC, it’s more visibly clear that models perform generally worse on recognizing contradictions compared to recognizing entailments, which echoes our observations in section 3 .
b: Contradiction was the label our models recognised most reliably, ahead of entailment.
label: contradiction
rationale: Worse on contradictions than entailments vs most reliable on contradiction, ahead of entailment. Note: sentence A contains comparison wording ('compared to'), so the comparison filter would skip this TRUE contradiction -- a natural test of that filter's recall cost.

a: For this reason, most large-scale NLI benchmarks follow the RD assumption during their annotation processes ( section 2 ).
b: Few large-scale NLI benchmarks have followed the RD assumption when annotating their examples.
label: contradiction
rationale: 'Most' benchmarks follow RD vs 'few' benchmarks followed RD.

a: We observe that in ambiguous cases, the annotators are more likely to label an example as neutral, while in the unambiguous case, raters are more likely to judge the hypothesis as entailed or contradicted by the premise.
b: When reference was ambiguous, annotators were least likely to choose the neutral label.
label: contradiction
rationale: Ambiguous cases: more likely neutral vs least likely neutral.

a: In light of the progress on inflation and the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.
b: Participants noted that the Committee had decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
label: contradiction
rationale: The Committee lowered the range vs kept it unchanged.

a: Given the significant progress made since the Committee first set its target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, a substantial majority of participants supported lowering the target range for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.
b: The Committee lowered the target range for the federal funds rate by a full percentage point from its previous level of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
label: contradiction
rationale: 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 minus a full point is 4-1/4 to 4-1/2, not 4-3/4 to 5 (which is a 50 bp cut). Requires arithmetic across fractional percentages.

a: In August, the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPI) was 2.5 percent, and core CPI inflation was 3.2 percent; both measures were well below their rates from a year ago.
b: In August, core CPI inflation ran 0.7 percentage point below the headline 12-month CPI change.
label: contradiction
rationale: Core 3.2 vs headline 2.5: core is 0.7 point ABOVE headline. Requires subtracting and checking the sign.

a: The ratio of job vacancies to unemployment edged down to 1.1 in August, a bit below its level just before the pandemic.
b: In August there were fewer job vacancies than unemployed workers.
label: contradiction
rationale: A vacancies-to-unemployment ratio of 1.1 means MORE vacancies than unemployed. Requires interpreting a ratio above 1.

a: With regard to the outlook for the labor market, participants noted that further cooling did not appear to be needed to help bring inflation back to 2 percent.
b: Participants agreed that a further softening of the labor market would be required to return inflation to 2 percent.
label: contradiction
rationale: Further cooling not needed vs further softening required, for the same goal.

a: Almost all participants judged that the risks to achieving the Committee's employment and inflation goals were roughly in balance.
b: Most participants judged that the risks to the Committee's goals were weighted heavily to the upside on inflation.
label: contradiction
rationale: 'Almost all' judged risks roughly balanced and 'most' judged them heavily weighted to one side: the two groups must overlap, so some participants would hold both views.

a: Rates on 30-year conforming residential mortgages and yields on agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) declined, on net, but continued to be elevated.
b: Mortgage rates rose on net over the intermeeting period.
label: contradiction
rationale: Mortgage rates declined on net vs rose on net.

a: Members concurred that there had been further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective but that inflation remained somewhat elevated.
b: Members concurred that inflation had already fallen below the Committee's 2 percent objective.
label: contradiction
rationale: Inflation still elevated (above 2 percent) vs already below 2 percent.

a: Both total and core PCE price inflation were expected to decline further as supply and demand in labor and product markets continued to move into better balance; by 2026, total and core inflation were expected to be 2 percent.
b: The staff's projected decline in PCE price inflation did not depend on supply and demand moving into better balance; it reflected lower energy prices alone.
label: contradiction
rationale: Decline attributed to supply and demand rebalancing vs explicitly not due to that, energy prices alone.

a: XIMAGE will maintain a 24 hour a day reporting facility to accept calls from MORPHO.
b: XIMAGE will accept calls from MORPHO only during regular business hours.
label: contradiction
rationale: 24-hour call acceptance vs business hours only.

a: XIMAGE undertake to have an engineer on site in Kuwait within 72 hours from the time the request was made, exclusive of the time required to arrange for travel and obtain the required documents, and the actual travel time itself.
b: XIMAGE's engineer is required on site in Kuwait no later than five days after the request, excluding travel arrangements and travel time.
label: contradiction
rationale: 72 hours is 3 days; the same on-site obligation is given two different deadlines. Requires converting hours to days.

a: Hourly rate for intervention is $125.00 (one hundred and twenty five Dollars).
b: Interventions will be charged at a rate of $150.00 per hour.
label: contradiction
rationale: Two different hourly rates for the same intervention.

a: MORPHO agrees that XIMAGE's total liability to MORPHO for any damages suffered in connection with, or arising out of, this Agreement or MORPHO's use of any documentation, product or service provided (or to be provided) hereunder, regardless of whether any such liability is based upon contract, tort or other basis, shall be limited to an amount not to exceed the basic Monthly Maintenance Charges, for a sixty (60) day term under this Agreement.
b: XIMAGE's total liability to MORPHO is capped at three months of basic Monthly Maintenance Charges.
label: contradiction
rationale: A sixty-day term of monthly charges is two months, not three. Requires converting days to months.

a: MORPHO shall pay all charges under this Agreement, including the total Annual Maintenance Charge, within thirty (30) days after receipt of a valid invoice from XIMAGE.
b: MORPHO shall pay the Annual Maintenance Charge within ninety (90) days after receipt of a valid invoice from XIMAGE.
label: contradiction
rationale: 30 days vs 90 days for the same payment.

a: The determination of the arbitrators shall not be subject to judicial review, provided however, that any award or determination rendered by the arbitrators may be enforced any court of jurisdiction.
b: Either party may appeal an arbitration award to a court, which may review the merits of the arbitrators' determination.
label: contradiction
rationale: No judicial review of the determination vs courts may review its merits.

a: The foregoing indemnification by XIMAGE shall not apply with respect to any claim based, in whole or part, on any modification of the Software made by any person other than XIMAGE.
b: XIMAGE's indemnification applies to all infringement claims, including those arising from modifications of the Software made by MORPHO.
label: contradiction
rationale: Indemnity excludes claims from others' modifications vs covers modifications made by MORPHO.

a: Each party agrees that the Confidential Information will be disclosed or made available only to those of its employees or consultants who have agreed to receive it under termes at least as restrictive as those specified in this Agreement.
b: Either party may share Confidential Information with its consultants without requiring any confidentiality undertaking from them.
label: contradiction
rationale: Disclosure only to consultants bound by restrictive terms vs to consultants with no undertaking at all. Requires seeing 'no undertaking' violates 'only those who agreed to restrictive terms'.

a: MORPHO may, at its option, return equipment to XIMAGE for repair.
b: Equipment may be returned for repair only when XIMAGE requests it.
label: contradiction
rationale: Return is at MORPHO's option vs only at XIMAGE's request. Requires seeing that 'only at XIMAGE's request' removes MORPHO's option.

a: The labor market has cooled from its formerly overheated state.
b: The labor market has heated up further and is now more overheated than it was a year ago.
label: contradiction
rationale: Cooled from overheated vs heated up further, more overheated.

a: GDP rose at an annual rate of 2.2 percent in the first half of the year, and available data point to a roughly similar pace of growth this quarter.
b: Growth has slowed sharply this quarter, to well below its pace in the first half of the year.
label: contradiction
rationale: Roughly similar pace this quarter vs well below the first-half pace.

a: The median projection for the unemployment rate in the SEP is 4.4 percent at the end of this year, four-tenths higher than projected in June.
b: In June, the SEP median had put the unemployment rate at 4.2 percent for the end of this year.
label: contradiction
rationale: 4.4 is four-tenths above 4.0, so the June projection was 4.0, not 4.2. Requires subtraction.

a: Inflation has eased substantially from a peak of 7 percent to an estimated 2.2 percent as of August.
b: Since its peak, inflation has fallen by roughly three percentage points.
label: contradiction
rationale: 7 minus 2.2 is a 4.8 point fall, not roughly 3. Requires subtraction.

a: Our economy is strong overall and has made significant progress toward our goals over the past two years.
b: Over the past two years, the economy has moved further away from our goals.
label: contradiction
rationale: Significant progress toward goals vs moved further away.

a: I think every single person on the Committee, if you asked them, what’s your level of certainty around that, they would say there’s a wide range where that could fall.
b: Several members of the Committee have told me they are quite certain where that level will fall.
label: contradiction
rationale: Every member would express wide uncertainty vs several members are quite certain.

a: As inflation has declined and the labor market has cooled, the upside risks to inflation have diminished, and the downside risks to employment have increased.
b: The diminished upside risks to inflation have nothing to do with the decline in inflation or the cooling of the labor market.
label: contradiction
rationale: Risks diminished as inflation declined and the labor market cooled vs explicitly unrelated to those developments.

a: We will continue to make our decisions meeting by meeting.
b: We have committed in advance to a fixed path of rate cuts over the next several meetings, regardless of incoming data.
label: contradiction
rationale: Deciding meeting by meeting vs pre-committing to a fixed multi-meeting path. Requires understanding what 'meeting by meeting' rules out.

a: You and your colleagues in your economic projections today see the unemployment rate climbing to 4.4 percent and staying there.
b: The Committee's projections show the unemployment rate peaking at 4.1 percent.
label: contradiction
rationale: Projected unemployment climbing to 4.4 percent vs peaking at 4.1 percent.
